source_review.notes: Checked all ten references. Current POSIX.1-2024 mutex types, owner-death, errors, synchronization, and destruction rules; Java SE 26 lock semantics; and Rust 1.98 guard and advisory poisoning behavior were verified against official specifications.

evidence: Reviewed owner, recursion depth, protected invariant, release/acquire, wait, hold, queue, and bounded-bypass notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: State and measurement symbols are defined with API-dependent cases explicit.

evidence: Executed six order-preserving lock/unlock histories and independently confirmed two serialized histories, four rejected overlaps, and one maximum owner.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts match exact stdout and the finite scope.

evidence: Re-derived non-reentrant and recursive owner-state transitions and the at-most-one-owner induction.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Owner safety is correctly separated from protected-state preservation and visibility.

evidence: Reviewed non-owner release, self-relock, recursive depth, try failure, timeout, panic, owner death, unfair admission, preempted owner, shutdown waiter, and process sharing.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Misuse, contention, recovery, and lifetime boundaries are covered.

evidence: Checked exclusive owner, valid access, authorized release, stable identity, state restoration, visibility, lock order, recovery, and destruction invariants.
invariant_checking.notes: Every transfer and abnormal exit retains a defined state obligation.

evidence: Reviewed owner-state induction, recursive depth, release/acquire publication, strict ordering, and poison/robust recovery arguments.
proof_review.notes: No primitive property is used to imply application correctness without its additional premises.

evidence: Audited spin, park, adaptive, fairness, queue-lock, priority protocol, robust, poison, process-shared, and try-lock claims.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Implementation and API-specific claims remain scoped and qualified.

evidence: Reproduced the annotated Python history enumeration with exact exit code, stdout, and empty stderr.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter disclaims implementation of blocking, memory ordering, fairness, recovery, or production behavior.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed distinctions among mutex ownership, exclusion, protected invariants, visibility, semaphore permits, condition predicates, fairness, progress, poisoning, and robust recovery.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed scoped guards, mutex types, open calls, spinning and parking, convoys, priority inversion, try/timed acquisition, multiple locks, owner failure, destruction, process sharing, and contention observability.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter moves from an inductive primitive model to concrete API and operational tradeoffs through ten examples and five aligned exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, railway, nuclear, real-time, hardware, cybersecurity, regulatory, or safety review is claimed. Finite enumeration and manual analysis do not prove a production mutex implementation, timing, fairness, recovery, or safety-critical deployment fitness.
